page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.20xlarge is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor offering a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz across 80 dedicated vCPUs. The instance is provisioned with 192.0 GB of system memory, which establishes an allocation ratio of 2.4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 25 Gbps.

Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent from this configuration, and no local disk storage is bundled. System persistence, root filesystems, and working data directories must be managed using attached cloud storage volumes. With 2.4 GB of RAM per core, the hardware layout prioritizes thread concurrency and central processing capability over extensive memory pools.

The absence of integrated local storage and accelerators focuses resource investment purely on processing capacity and network throughput. This configuration delivers consistent execution environments for multi-threaded, CPU-bound workloads. Typical suitable deployment scenarios include distributed continuous integration builds, high-throughput web service clusters, batch data transformation, and parallel numerical simulations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.20xlarge is a compute-focused instance in the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor and an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. It features 80 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of memory, yielding a ratio of 2.4 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. There is no bundled local storage and no GPU hardware present, requiring workloads to rely on network-attached storage for persistent data. This architectural profile directs resources toward raw central processing power and network throughput rather than expansive memory or local disk I/O. As such, ecs.hfc6.20xlarge is suited for compute-intensive workloads that demand substantial parallel processing, including large-scale build pipelines, distributed batch jobs, financial modeling, scientific computing, and high-traffic web application tiers.
